logline: You're broke, you owe the wrong people, and you just took a job driving a car you shouldn't ask questions about. Every day ends with a choice. The comments make it. Your stats keep score.

format.pov: Second person: 'You owe forty thousand dollars to the wrong people.'
structure: Open with last vote: a stamp on screen ('OPENED · 64%') + the consequence.
End on a hard A/B choice with real trade-offs (cash vs heat vs trust).
format.stats: HUD shows CASH (dollars, can be negative), HEAT (police/attention %), TRUST (how much the crew trusts you %). Every choice moves at least one stat. If HEAT hits 100% or TRUST hits 0%, the season ends badly; a payoff above +$100,000 with HEAT under 50% is the good ending.
format.seasons: A season is ~20-30 days. Then a fresh story in the same city.
format.narration_style: Gritty, fast, punchy. Short sentences, present-day slang kept light. One keyword per sentence in *asterisks* (yellow).

voices._note: Narrator: am_puck blended with am_onyx (deeper, gritty). Never add echo/reverb to voices.

voting_rules.how: Each comment = one vote for the first option it names (keyword, label or letter A/B). Show the split as a stamp at the start of the next part, e.g. 'OPENED · 64%'.
voting_rules.cameos: Commenters asking to be in it can appear as side characters (another driver, a bartender, a cop) with their handle on a name tag. Same safety rules as the other channels.

safety_rules: Crime-thriller tone, not instructional: never explain how to commit real crimes.
No graphic violence (cut away), no glamorizing drugs, no real gangs, people or places.

scene_types.bg: street | lot | car (add more in render/players/crime.js)
scene_types.hud: {cash, heat, trust}: values animate from the previous scene
